text:
Some of us decided to take the cheaper route when purchasing our MK6s and ended up with halogens. I as well as others regret that decision and are searching for opportunities to ditch the halogens for OEM xenons. I did this conversion but left out the cornering and auto leveling geature to save about $2k.

Needed to complete the swap:
-OEM xenon housings
-Ballasts
-Bulbs
-Xenon pin adapter harness (OEM+, Kufatec or ECS tuning)
-VCDS (vagcom)
-Highline CECM*

*In order to have functional LEDs with the oem setup you will need to purchase a highline CECM if yours ends in anything other than 087.

Start with removing the grille, (4) screws at the top and gently remove each of the tabs at the bottom of the grille. With the grille removed you have access to the (2) screws holding the bumper in place. You will also need to remove (5) screws from each side of the fenders from the top of the bumper down to the bottom. Next, dependin on whether or not you have the votex spoiler installed you will need to remove the screws holding the bottom of the bumper in place which can range from (8-14) I believe. With all the mounting points removed, pull the bumper away from the car. I just removed it and placed it on a towel in front of the car. You will then remove the (3) screws holding each headlight in place. After removing the headlight harness from the backside of the headlight you should be able to pull the factory halogens out of the bumper.

Install the xenon headlights and screw them back into place. Make sure the (2) tabs at the bottom of the headlights as well as the track sysyem that lines them up with the bumper. With the headlight plug adapter harness, you will plug the female end into the factory wiring and the male end into the xenon headlights. I have an APR intake so I tucked the harness just above the radiator and ziptied it in place to make sure it wasn't in the way of the fan or radiator. After that, just install everything in reversal of removal.

Enjoy!

Disclaimer: These are the steps I followed when converting the halogens on my 2011 GTI to non-LED xenon headlights. I am not responsible for any damage you may occur during this conversion.

For those looking to make their xenons and high beams work with a mid line CECM and non-LED headlights, follow the following steps from page 9 & 10:

You will need to go to Central Electronics with VAGCOM, go to byte 17 and uncheck bit 2.

As requested, provided by a member from Page 9 is the pinout:

I don't have wire colors, just do one at a time
Halogen Pin -> Xenon Pin
1 -> 4
4 -> 12
5 -> 5 & 7 (additional ground to 7)
6 -> 6
8 -> 11 (high beams)
9 -> 9
10 -> 10
